title: Reconciliation queued on an in-memory executor is acknowledged with HTTP 200
failureScenario: Between executor.submit at StripeWebhookService.java:56 and the task's first instruction on the pool thread, the JVM is stopped (deploy, OOMKilled). The provider has already received HTTP 200 (BillingWebhookController.java:36), so the event is never redelivered; the reconciliation never happens. The dropped Future also hides any exception the task throws.

evidence.claim: The reconciliation is handed to an executor and the returned Future is discarded.
The executor is an in-memory pool with an unbounded queue; nothing survives a restart.
The provider is told the webhook succeeded before the queued task has run.

mitigationsChecked.name: durable hand-off (outbox, queue, job table) before acknowledgement
graceful drain of the executor on shutdown
provider-side redelivery after 2xx
mitigationsChecked.where: Stripe redelivers only on timeout or non-2xx

recommendation: Persist the reconciliation request (outbox row or a job table) inside T1 and let a scheduled worker or the SQS consumer execute it; or move the reconciliation into the SQS consumer path. Replace the raw pool with a Spring TaskExecutor configured with waitForTasksToCompleteOnShutdown.
verification: Submit a webhook with the executor's threads blocked, send SIGTERM to the JVM, restart: the reconciliation for that event never runs and no error is logged.
Unit: assert that handle() does not return before the reconciliation is durably recorded.

verifiedBy.note: Independent agent could not find any durable record of the task; mitigations re-checked.

title: SQS send inside the receipt transaction (dual write, no outbox)
failureScenario: sqsTemplate.send at line 53 succeeds, then the commit of T1 fails (constraint violation, connection loss). The invoice event is published for a receipt that was never stored; Stripe retries the webhook and a second message is sent for the same event.

evidence.claim: handle() runs in one local JPA transaction.
The DB insert is part of T1.
The SQS send happens before T1 commits; SqsTemplate is not a transactional resource.

mitigationsChecked.name: consumer-side idempotency that would absorb the duplicate

recommendation: Write an outbox row in T1 and publish from a relay; or publish from an AFTER_COMMIT listener and accept the small at-most-once window with reconciliation.
verification: Make the commit fail after the send (e.g. a unique-violation on provider_event_id) and observe the message on care-invoice-events with no billing_event_receipt row.

title: Webhook is not idempotent: redelivery creates duplicate receipts and messages
failureScenario: Stripe redelivers the same event after a timeout or non-2xx. handle() inserts a second receipt, sends a second SQS message and queues a second reconciliation; nothing checks provider_event_id first.

evidence.claim: Insert without a prior lookup by provider event id.
A lookup exists but is never called from handle().

mitigationsChecked.name: lookup by provider event id before processing
unique constraint on provider_event_id
mitigationsChecked.where: no migration or DDL in the repository was inspected

recommendation: Insert the receipt with a unique constraint on provider_event_id and return 200 on conflict; only then send and reconcile.
verification: POST the same signed payload twice; expect one receipt row and one SQS message.

verifiedBy.note: Confidence stays MEDIUM: the DB-level unique constraint was not checked.

title: Provider charge executed inside the invoice DB transaction
failureScenario: createCharge at InvoiceService.java:34 succeeds (money moves), then the commit of the invoice transaction fails. The AFTER_ROLLBACK listener only logs. The customer is charged with no invoice row; the SQS redelivery then charges again.

evidence.claim: The method runs in a DB transaction.
The remote charge happens before commit, holding the DB connection.

evidence.snippet: log.error("Invoice {} rolled back after provider charge for customer {}",
evidence.claim: The rollback path only logs; no compensation.

mitigationsChecked.name: charge after commit (outbox or two-phase: reserve, commit, charge, confirm)

recommendation: Commit the invoice as PENDING first, charge with an idempotency key derived from the invoice id, then mark CHARGED in a second transaction; reconcile PENDING invoices by a scheduled job.
verification: Make the commit fail after createCharge (e.g. a trigger that rejects the update) and observe a charge with no invoice.

title: SQS consumer creates a new invoice and charge on every redelivery
failureScenario: SQS is at-least-once. A visibility timeout (amplified by the missing HTTP timeouts, F-1a2b3c07) redelivers the message while the first attempt is still running; both attempts insert an invoice with a fresh random id and both call createCharge.

evidence.claim: Unconditional insert; no lookup by provider event id.

mitigationsChecked.name: dedupe by provider event id before insert
FIFO queue with content-based deduplication
mitigationsChecked.where: queue configuration is outside the repository

recommendation: Derive the invoice id (or a unique natural key) from the provider event id and insert-if-absent; skip the charge when the row already exists.
verification: Deliver the same message twice; expect one invoice and one charge.

title: Charge request carries no idempotency key
failureScenario: Any retry of createCharge (client retry, redelivery, or a timeout after the provider has processed the request) charges the payer again; the provider cannot deduplicate.

evidence.snippet: return restTemplate.postForObject(baseUrl + "/v1/charges", new HttpEntity<>(body, headers), ChargeResult.class);
evidence.claim: Only Authorization is set on the request; no Idempotency-Key header.

recommendation: Send Idempotency-Key = invoice id (stable across retries).
verification: Replay the same createCharge call; the provider must return the first charge.

title: RestTemplate without connect/read timeouts on the provider call
failureScenario: The provider hangs. The SQS listener thread blocks indefinitely inside the DB transaction; the visibility timeout expires and the message is redelivered while the first attempt is still in flight.

mitigationsChecked.name: timeouts on the request factory or RestTemplateBuilder

recommendation: Build the RestTemplate with RestTemplateBuilder.setConnectTimeout/setReadTimeout, and bound the listener's processing time below the queue visibility timeout.
verification: Point baseUrl at a blackhole address; the listener thread must fail within the configured timeout.

title: Poison message is redelivered until retention expires
failureScenario: A malformed payload makes readTree throw on every delivery; without a DLQ or error handler the message is retried until the queue retention period ends, consuming listener capacity.

evidence.claim: Parsing throws for malformed input; the exception leaves the listener.

mitigationsChecked.name: redrive policy / DLQ on the queue
mitigationsChecked.where: queue configuration is outside the repository

recommendation: Configure a redrive policy with maxReceiveCount and alert on the DLQ; catch parse errors and park the message.
verification: Send a non-JSON body; count redeliveries.

title: Invoice e-mail sent after commit with no retry or record
failureScenario: The AFTER_COMMIT listener calls the mail service once; if that call fails or the JVM stops between commit and listener, the e-mail is never sent and nothing records that it is missing. The invoice itself is safe.

evidence.claim: Runs AFTER_COMMIT by default, outside the transaction (correct placement).
Single attempt; no retry, no notification record.

mitigationsChecked.name: retry or outbox for the notification

recommendation: Acceptable for a notification. If the e-mail is contractual, record a notification row in the transaction and send from a retrying worker.
verification: Stop the mail service, issue an invoice, restart it: no e-mail is ever sent.
